blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: formar el present perfect con have / has + participio
decir cuánto tiempo dura algo con for y since

blocks.text: El present perfect es have (o has con he, she, it) más el participio (past participle), como he visto en español. En los verbos regulares es la forma en -ed: worked, played. Los irregulares tienen una tercera forma propia: go – went – gone.

blocks.label: verbo irregular
examples: I have seen that film twice.
He visto esa película dos veces.
She has never seen the sea.
Ella nunca ha visto el mar.
We have seen a lot of Spain.
You have seen the new office.

blocks.title: have = haber, no tener
blocks.text: Aquí have funciona como haber: he ido = I have gone, ha venido = She has come. Y como en español, el participio no cambia nunca. No confundas este have con tener: I have seen it es lo he visto, no lo tengo visto.

blocks.title: ¿been o gone?
blocks.text: He has gone to Spain: se ha ido y sigue allí. He has been to Spain: ha estado allí y ya ha vuelto.
Con el present perfect cuentas lo que has hecho alguna vez en la vida, sin decir cuándo.

head: Inglés
Español
rows: Have you ever been to London?
Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
She has visited Spain three times.
Ella ha estado tres veces en España.

blocks.title: El lugar en la frase
blocks.text: just y already van entre have y el participio: I have just arrived. (Acabo de llegar.) yet va al final: Have you called her yet?
Para algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue ahora, se usa el present perfect con for (un periodo) o since (un punto de partida).

head: Ejemplo
Español
rows: I've lived here for ten years.
Vivo aquí desde hace diez años.
How long have you known her?

blocks.title: Presente en español, present perfect en inglés
blocks.text: Vivo aquí desde hace diez años y Llevo diez años aquí van en presente en español. El inglés usa el present perfect: I have lived here for ten years. I live here since ten years es incorrecto. Recuerda: desde hace = for, desde = since.

rows: I have went to the shop.
I have gone to the shop.
Después de have va el participio: gone, no went.
Algo que sigue hasta ahora: present perfect.
I have lived here since ten years.
I have lived here for ten years.
Have you ever went to Rome?
Have you ever been to Rome?
Después de have va el participio.
I have known her for years.

blocks.text: Completa con el present perfect o con la palabra que falta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.full: I have seen that film three times.
She has been to Spain many times.
Have you ever been to Scotland?

items.q: We have ______ arrived. We're still taking our coats off.
items.full: We have just arrived. We're still taking our coats off.
Have you finished your homework yet?
I've lived in this town since 2018.
They've been married for twenty years.
He has never eaten Indian food.

items.q: I ______ my keys. I can't find them.
items.full: I have lost my keys. I can't find them.
How long have you known her?

items.q: She has ______ left. She went an hour ago.
items.full: She has already left. She went an hour ago.
They haven't written the letter yet.

items.q: Vivo aquí desde hace cinco años.
items.a: I have lived here for five years.
Have you ever been to London?
